name: Why is my water heater not producing hot water?

mainEntity.name: Why is my water heater not producing hot water?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your water heater isn't producing hot water, several issues could be at fault. For electric water heaters, a tripped breaker, faulty heating elements, or a malfunctioning thermostat are common culprits. Gas water heaters might have a pilot light that has gone out, a problem with the thermocouple, or a faulty gas control valve. Sediment buildup can also reduce efficiency. It's best to have a qualified technician diagnose the exact cause.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common issues include tripped breakers, faulty heating elements or thermostats for electric heaters, or a pilot light/thermocouple problem for gas heaters.
